did_you_know.text: The verse places the instructions on the plains of Moab — east of the Jordan near the Jericho area; it shows the laws were given just before entering Canaan.

The Levites do not get a large territorial inheritance like the other tribes, but cities with surrounding plots — a solution that links their public role to their presence among the tribal communities.
A radius of one thousand amot is specified around the city wall for the Levites’ plots; this measure creates a defined zone for agriculture and grazing.
The next verse gives different dimensions — two thousand amot in each direction, placing the city at the center of a larger area; scholars understand this as different zones surrounding the city.
The chapter states there are forty-eight Levitical cities in total — a combination of service cities and cities of refuge, distributing the Levites throughout the land.
'Cities of refuge' are towns intended to protect someone who killed accidentally from the blood-avenger; it’s a legal institution that distinguishes accident from intentional murder.
The text distinguishes by type of weapon: if someone is struck with an iron tool and dies, it is treated as murder and punishable by death — this distinction aims to assess guilt and intent.
When the act is done out of hatred (a push or shove), it is regarded as intentional murder — motive is judged alongside the outcome.
The community must return the fugitive to the city of refuge and keep him there until the high priest’s death; the legal status also depends on the lifetime of the high priest.
If the avenger finds the fugitive outside the city boundaries — he may kill him without guilt; the protection applies only within the city’s limits.
A central legal principle here is: you cannot impose death based on a single witness — two or more witnesses are required for serious offenses.
